one_question: Must an integrated complex organ evolve as an integrated unit?
working_answer: Phenotypic integration can be repeatedly reconstructed from components whose coupling is not persistently shared across ecology, history and genomic inheritance.
rejected_or_demoted_framings: ecological modules necessarily align with genomic modules
combinatorial reuse alone is the Nature-scale novelty
accelerated evolutionary rate is a prerequisite for the main mechanism

competing_models.whole_organ_fixed_integration: all admitted constructs inherit through one shared genomic state
competing_models.phenotypic_module_inheritance: one genomic state per frozen Azami phenotypic module; constructs within each module share that inherited state
competing_models.reconfigurable_integration: component genomic states are not constrained to the frozen phenotypic-module partition and can reassemble

nature_kill_shot: On untouched validation individuals, the reconfigurable model predicts multi-construct phenotypes better than the frozen phenotypic-module model, and prospectively registered natural genomic mosaics correctly predict new colour × anthesis-orientation combinations.
primary_falsifier: Model M predicts untouched phenotypes as well as Model R, or Model F predicts as well as both, or prospective mosaics fail to predict component states.
figure_contract: Fig1: present integration plus failure of one fixed ecological partition and robust component-specific ecological anchors
Fig2: repeated, unequal-depth, nonsynchronized component histories
Fig3: untouched prediction comparison of whole-organ F, frozen phenotypic-module M, and reconfigurable R genomic architectures
Fig4: prospectively registered natural genomic mosaics and out-of-sample component-combination prediction
Fig5: representative function-to-fitness chain showing coherent reproductive performance after component reassembly
claim_boundaries: cross-level modularity mismatch is not itself claimed as unprecedented
historical nonsynchrony is not genetic independence
genomic modularity requires same-individual dense data and reference-stable inference
species-wide state multiplicity is not a verified within-population combinatorial substrate
diversification_context: The young radiation supplies a stringent shallow-timescale test and repeated component histories; Fig3 R support does not by itself establish that reconfigurability caused an elevated diversification rate.
novelty_target: Directly compete a predeclared phenotypic-module inheritance model against a complexity-matched module-breaking genomic model in the same natural individuals, using untouched phenotype prediction and prospectively registered natural mosaics as the discriminator.
nature_core_success: The central evolutionary-unit claim is closed by FIG3_R_STRONG plus the preregistered Fig4 prospective-mosaic criterion. Fig5 is not an AND prerequisite for that claim.
fig5_extension: If the functional/fitness chain succeeds, the claim extends from reconfigurable inheritance to reassembly compatible with coherent reproductive function. If it fails or is not yet executed, do not reinterpret the genomic result; simply keep the functional extension closed.
